title: Move faster across a magnetic field
hook: Change particle speed and predict magnetic-force magnitude.
misconception: magnetic-force magnitude stays fixed when particle speed doubles.
objective: Apply F = abs(q)vB to compare magnetic-force magnitude when particle speed changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a fixed charge moving perpendicular to a fixed uniform magnetic field, F = abs(q)vB. When particle speed doubles, magnetic-force magnitude becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model F = abs(q)vB; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a fixed charge moving perpendicular to a fixed uniform magnetic field, with a nonzero initial result. If particle speed triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on magnetic-force magnitude?
recall.why: Apply F = abs(q)vB under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
